definitions.explanation: Planning something secretly, typically with negative or self-serving intent. Implies underhanded or manipulative planning behind the scenes.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{裏|うら}で{画策|かくさく}していた。
examples.english: He was scheming behind the scenes.

examples.japanese: {政権|せいけん}{交代|こうたい}を{画策|かくさく}する{動|うご}きがあった。
examples.english: There were moves to plot a change of government.

examples.japanese: {競合|きょうごう}{他社|たしゃ}を{追|お}い{落|お}とそうと{画策|かくさく}したが、{結局|けっきょく}{自分|じぶん}たちの{評判|ひょうばん}を{落|お}とす{結果|けっか}になった。
examples.english: They schemed to bring down a rival company, but it ended up damaging their own reputation.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always carries a negative connotation. Used to describe secret, self-serving plans or political maneuvering. Functions as a する verb: {画策|かくさく}する (to scheme, to plot).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {計画|けいかく}: plan — neutral, no negative connotation
- {画策|かくさく}: scheme, plot — implies secrecy and negative intent
- {陰謀|いんぼう}: conspiracy — stronger, implies larger-scale plotting

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {裏|うら}で{画策|かくさく}する: scheme behind the scenes
- {密|ひそ}かに{画策|かくさく}する: secretly plot
- クーデターを{画策|かくさく}する: plot a coup
